ads.title: How to choose the right whey
ads.body: Confused about which whey protein to buy? Start here. Step 1 - Check the ingredients before anything else. Protein powder should be protein, not a chemical cocktail. If the label has artificial sweeteners like Ace K or Sucralose or vague terms like "natural flavours" - those aren't as harmless as they sound. Find something cleaner. Step 2 - Concentrate or isolate? Both come from the same source. Concentrate is creamier, a bit heavier. Isolate is filtered further - lighter, lower in lactose, easier to digest. If you're lactose intolerant, isolate is the better call. If you want the best of both, a 70:30 blend of isolate and concentrate is a solid middle ground like our Light Cocoa Protein Powder. That's your whey sorted.
I’m not here for protein debates. Pure whey vs real-food add-ons, both can work. What are you choosing today?

Protein ke peeche itne saare chemicals? You don’t need them! Protein powders are only for ‘men trying to build bulky muscles’. They’re ‘steroids’. They’re not for me. Why do all these protein myths continue to exist? They exist because most protein powders are a black box. An unnecessary concoction of harmful chemicals. And then every week a new report finds amino spiking or heavy metals, further solidifying our fears. This needs to change. You parents, your spouse, and you - everyone needs more protein. But it won’t happen until we take the protein conversation away from gyms and into our living rooms. And it definitely won’t happen if protein powders remain a black box. Hence, this film. The lyrics acknowledge the problem. The iconic song (and the beautiful men dancing to it) hopefully brings down barriers to having the conversation. And our 100% clean protein powders (we hope with all our heart) enable the change. Share this. And tell us how you, or a loved one, finally got started on your protein journey.
